# Chat instructions

- Always consider all opened editors as context for your session. If you have to guess the content of a class, ask first if that class already exists and for said class to be added to your context.
- When writing code, always add just before said code the full path and name of the file which will include said code.
- When writing code, alway print first the full pathname of the file which will host said code: full absolute path or relative path from the workspace root of the project.
- When asked for a commit message, always write a conventional commit message composed of:
  - a "type(scope): title" in 52 chars or less
  - a body with lines of 80 chars of less, composed of:
    - a "Why" section in which you explain why the changes listed in the next section needed to be made
    - a "What" section in which you list the changes made
- When writing an answer in markdown, always use only one space after an ordered or non-ordered list marker. And make sure to insert an empty line before the first item of a list (ordered or not-ordered).  
  Do not use `1.  **Implement New Elements**` (two or more space after the '1.' list marker), but `1. **Implement New Elements**`.  
  Do not use '`* xx`' for unordered list item, but '`- xx`' (dash for unordered list item).  
  Do not use 4 spaces for sub-list, always 2 spaces more than the parent item list.

If your answer includes those words (outside of code snippets), use the technique “BBQ-it” (source book - Make It Punchy): take a word or phrase, and then imagine how 2 blokes at a bbq would talk about it. For instance: “optimise vehicle location” could become ‘know exactly where your vehicles are”. Replace them with simpler, more direct language. For example, instead of "leverage," you could say "use." Instead of "optimize," you might say "make better."
